Done - also simplified the API by replacing `getInstrumentationEnabled(String)` / `isInstrumentationEnabled(String)` with a single `isInstrumentationEnabled(Iterable<String>, boolean)` method and moved the logic from `InstrumentationModuleInstaller` into `AgentDistributionConfig`.

Instead of always returning defaults (which would silently hide bootstrap ordering bugs at runtime), I went with a two-phase approach:

- Added `AgentDistributionConfig.expectInitialization()` which is called early in `AgentInstaller` bootstrap
- `get()` behavior depends on context:
  - **Agent running** (`expectInitialization()` was called): throws if `set()` hasn't been called yet — catches ordering bugs
  - **Agent not running** (Gradle `byteBuddyJava` build, tests): returns a default instance — no crash

This way we stay strict at runtime (as you intended in e6e9e27) but are lenient during builds where no agent is present.

threads.body:
AI thinks this might be a bug, can you check and/or add a test to confirm?

`Environment.getProperty(key, List.class)` doesn't reassemble indexed YAML list properties.

When a user writes:

```yaml
distribution:
  spring_starter:
    instrumentation:
      enabled:
        - spring_web
        - tomcat
```

Spring flattens this to `enabled[0]=spring_web`, `enabled[1]=tomcat` — but `getProperty("...enabled", List.class)` looks for an exact key match, finds nothing, and returns `emptyList()`. Only flat comma-separated values work (e.g. `enabled=spring_web,tomcat`).

The existing tests all use `withPropertyValues()` (flat strings), so they don't catch this. Use Spring Boot's `Binder` API instead, which properly handles indexed properties.

replies.body: Good point - I guess my AI will add a test for it - once it processes your (AIs?) comment :smile:

Fixed — switched to Spring Boot's `Binder` API in `EarlyConfig.bindList()` which handles both indexed (`enabled[0]=spring_web`) and comma-separated formats. Added two new tests with indexed properties to confirm.
